name: Baby Shit Green
lede: Baby Shit Green is a dull olive-green, the greener sibling of [[baby-shit-brown|Baby Shit Brown]] that the 2010 xkcd color survey's respondents named as a separate cluster.

sections.title: A crowd name for a plain comparison
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Who typed it first is undocumented [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a strong yellow green, about 3.9 units off, with Munsell notation 3.0GY 5.8/8.6 [1].

The closest look-alike in our data is [[baby-poop-green|Baby Poop Green]], just 2.2 units away, with [[pea-soup|Pea Soup]], [[avocado|Avocado]] and [[ugly-green|Ugly Green]] also close [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds this olive-green in 21 of them, about 0.09 percent, rarer than 63 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 4.7 times the expected rate for that century (8 of 1,674 paintings from then), and inside a painting it is most often an accent, 59 percent of the time, by lightness rank rather than raw area [2].

The earliest match in our archive is dated 1801, 209 years before the name itself appears in 2010 [2]. Our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first, and the match is only a look-alike hue, not proof the name or a matching dye existed then [2].
